_: EP 16 — SNS + SQS. The EP 15 construction, unchanged, because it works: one continuous canvas the camera travels on a serpentine, stations rather than slides, one stroke-icon family so no box is ever a labelled rectangle, the DESIGN.md marketing surface (bloom field, hero card, product panels, the box pattern), and a continuity chip that follows ONE message from published to deleted. Nine stations instead of thirteen — this is a 90-second episode, so the arc is tighter and every station carries exactly one idea. EVERY NUMBER ON SCREEN IS REAL AND SOURCED (docs.aws.amazon.com sqs/sns developer guides): visibility timeout defaults to 30 seconds and maxes at 12 hours; retention defaults to 4 days and maxes at 14; max message size is 256 KB; long polling waits up to 20 seconds; SQS standard requests are $0.40 per million after the first million free; FIFO queues do 300 messages a second, 3,000 with batches of 10, and dedupe on a 5-minute window; standard queues are at-least-once with best-effort ordering; a redrive policy moves a message to the dead-letter queue after maxReceiveCount receives.
title: Shout Once.
subtitle: SNS fans it out. SQS holds it until you are ready.
hook: One publish. Many queues. Nobody waiting on anybody.

The continuity is the construction and the cue set; what changes per episode is the value journey and which bloom carries each act. EP15 ran cream → canvas → cool → canvas → saturated. EP16 runs saturated → canvas → dark (the failure act) → canvas → saturated.

_vo: Nine lines. Directive throughout — the narrator hands you the thing in order. Definition then consequence, one clause a sentence, and an instruction verb opening eight of the nine.

vo.text:
Watch what a direct call costs you. Five services to notify…
and any one of them can fail your write.
Publish once, to a topic. SNS copies that message into every queue subscribed to it.
Read what arrives. A body, message attributes, and a receipt handle you need to delete it.

Filter at the subscription. A policy keeps events out of the queue…
instead of out of your code.
The queue is a shock absorber. Producers spike, consumers drain, and nothing is dropped in between.
Take a message and it goes invisible for thirty seconds. Miss that window, and it comes back.
Set maxReceiveCount. After that many failed reads, the message moves to a dead-letter queue.
Standard queues are at-least-once, and unordered. Need strict order? Use FIFO, and pay in throughput.
Turn on long polling. Twenty seconds of wait removes the empty receives, and most of your bill.

_shots: No Kling in this register. EP15 proved the marketing-surface construction carries a full episode on graphics alone: the bloom field is the texture, the grain is per-frame, and the depth comes from real product panels rather than footage. Nothing to generate, nothing to grade.
